newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa seen needing rate cuts to avoid recession.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa seen needing rate cuts to avoid recession.

text.p: The South African economy may slip into recession unless there is a rapid easing in interest rates, Credit Guarantee Insurance Corp of Africa Ltd said on Tuesday.

The credit risk insurer said in a statement that recent economic data showed South Africa's economic growth was slowing and the country had a worsening trend of liquidations and debt judgments against private individuals and businesses.

"At this rate, liquidations (of companies) in 1997 appear certain of surpassing 1994's record of 3,273," said Luke Doig, Credit Guarantee Insurance's senior manager for economic and investment services.
His company's estimates showed that debt judgments against individuals could exceed 4.1 billion rand and for businesses 680 million rand.
"The issue now does not relate to when the South African Reserve Bank will relent but how quickly the second and third cuts will eventuate," Doig said in the statement.
"If not before the start of the second quarter of 1998, growth could struggle to attain two percent next year," Luke Doig said.
Even with interest rate cuts, debt judgments could continue to escalate for more than two years, Doig said.
"The impact this will have on private expenditure is likely to be marked and we may be headed for more than just a short-lived or mild recession," he added.

Rate-cut speculation has been mounting in South Africa in recent weeks following the relaxation of exchange controls on July 1. That easing proceeded without triggering an immediate flight of funds, which some analysts had feared.
South Africa's prime interest rate currently stands at 20.25 percent and the bank rate is 17 percent.
